gap: No result ChatGPT got that I could read states that RTINGS bench-tested the MCHOSE Ace 60 Pro and confirmed it uses its full 8,000 Hz polling "without any latency-related bottlenecks", while saying it cannot verify the advertised 128,000 Hz scan rate; none of the other budget candidates, the Gamakay boards included, has a named-lab latency test I could find.
standout_why: Compared against five pages. The cited RTINGS research page (2025-07-31) already makes the general point: rapid trigger boards it tested sit between 1 ms and 18 ms release latency and the differences are too small to matter; it names no budget board from ChatGPT's answer. mechanicalkeyboard.net (rank 1), setupinsider.com (rank 3) and keyboardverdict.com (rank 2) carry only maker specs, no lab latency, and none mentions Gamakay. The cited PC Gamer Hall effect guide could not be read (the fetch returned only navigation, the proxy returned 403), so I cannot rule out that it carries a measurement. The per-model RTINGS finding is new against the pages read, but it is qualitative: RTINGS locks the millisecond figures behind membership, so there is no side-by-side number table to publish.
decides: It confirms ChatGPT's pick rather than changing it: the MCHOSE Ace 60 Pro is the only budget candidate whose latency and 8,000 Hz polling a named lab has checked, with RTINGS noting it is wired-only and fairly loud. The Gamakay NS68, NS75 and TK75HE V2 have no named-lab measurement I could find, so the page cannot claim measured parity for them. RTINGS's research conclusion (any rapid trigger board in the 1 to 18 ms range will do) supports choosing on price, layout and connection modes instead, which is the only ground on which the NS68 ($36.79 wired, $39.99 tri-mode per the brief's 2026-11-21 store read) can place. This angle alone does not carry the page.
